analytics.adminSetupTitle: What an administrator needs to do
analytics.adminSetupBody: Analytics runs on Metabase, which is open source and self-hosted, so no licence is needed and no figure leaves this deployment. Start it with `docker compose --profile analytics up -d metabase`, create the read-only database role with `make bi-role`, build a dashboard, then publish it for embedding and set the Metabase variables. Until then, an analyst can point any SQL tool at the read-only schema below.
analytics.connectionLead: A read-only schema an analyst can build reports against today, with Metabase, DBeaver, psql, R or pandas.

cropYield.title: El Niño impacts & crop recommendations
cropYield.intro: What El Niño did to tef, wheat and maize in each altitude belt over the {firstYear}–{lastYear} record, what that implies for planting, and what a model fitted on the same record expects next season. The record and the model are separate claims and are reported separately.
cropYield.sourceDataset: last year of the crop record
cropYield.matrixTitle: Expected yield by crop and altitude belt
cropYield.matrixDesc: Quintals per hectare (1 quintal = 100 kg). Each belt is a zone-wide average, never one farm.
cropYield.ensoDesc: Each bar is the expected yield minus the same row with Niño 3.4 set to zero, so it isolates the model's whole climate response. The bars are small because the model leans on last year's yield.
cropYield.limitsTitle: What this model can and cannot say
cropYield.limitsDesc: Carried from the trained artifact, not written by hand.
cropYield.candidatesDesc: Trained on {trainFrom}–{trainTo}, scored on {testFrom}–{testTo} ({rows} observations). Lower RMSE is better.
cropYield.leansOnDesc: Share of the gradient-boosted model's gain, feature by feature.
cropYield.notPlotLevel: Belt average, not a plot-level prediction

impact.title: El Niño impact on crop yields (%)
impact.cardTitle: Measured over the record, not predicted
impact.cardDesc: Each crop-belt series is detrended first, then El Niño years are compared with all other years. The number is percentage points away from that series’ own trend.
impact.caption: El Niño effect on yield by crop and altitude belt, with p-values
impact.legendLoss: Yield below trend in El Niño years
impact.takeawayOverall: Across all crops and belts, El Niño years sit {pct}% below trend.
impact.takeawayWorst: {crop} in the {zone} belt is hit hardest, {pct}% below trend.
impact.takeawayBest: {crop} holds up best, and is the only crop above trend in the {zone} belt.
impact.takeawaySignificance: On {years} El Niño years in {from}–{to}, {significant} of {total} cells reach p < 0.05 — the record shows a direction, not a proven effect size.
impact.elNinoYears: El Niño years in the record: {years}.

belts.title: Recommended crop by altitude belt
belts.cardDesc: For each belt, the crop whose yield held up best in El Niño years. Where even the best crop lost ground, the card says "least loss" rather than a gain.
belts.gains: +{pct}% above trend in El Niño years
belts.caution: Cultivate {crop} with caution in the {zone} belt — the worst pairing in the record, {pct}% below trend in El Niño years — unless supported by irrigation, soil moisture conservation and drought-tolerant varieties.

actions.title: Recommended actions
actions.forecasts: Use the seasonal outlook to guide planting dates.
actions.irrigation: Expand irrigation and soil moisture conservation.
actions.caution: Cultivate {crop} with caution in the {zone} belt.

timeline.heading: The record and what follows it
timeline.description: Belt-average yields over Niño 3.4, {firstYear} to {throughYear}. Yields are observed to {yieldYear} and Niño 3.4 to {ensoYear}; the seasons between them are projected under the ENSO that actually happened. Only the shaded years rest on an assumption.
timeline.scenarioLabel: ENSO state assumed after the observed record
timeline.assumedFrom: Assumed from {year}: no candidate beat climatology past {months} months
timeline.footnote: Yields observed to {yieldYear}, Niño 3.4 to {ensoYear}. Projected seasons are predicted from the season before them, because last year's yield is an input: the error compounds and the series settles on a level. Holdout RMSE {rmse} q/ha.
timeline.unavailable: The crop-yield model is not loaded on this deployment, so the timeline cannot be drawn.

pricing.title: Pricing & stakeholders
pricing.intro: What each kind of stakeholder pays to use the platform, in birr. A price is never edited in place: changing one closes the rate in force and opens a new version, so an agreement signed last year still resolves to the rate it was signed at.
pricing.cardDesc: All amounts in {currency}. The annual rate is what contracts are written at; the others follow from it.
pricing.caption: Price per stakeholder type, by billing period
pricing.supersedeNote: Amounts in {currency}. Saving supersedes the current price from the date above; the old rate stays readable in the history.
pricing.structure: Three rules hold across every paying tier: monthly is a tenth of the annual rate, so paying by the year costs ten months rather than twelve; the daily rate is the annual one over 365; and the perpetual licence is four years. They are commercial decisions, not rounding.
